status2026.detail: On the APS 'Beamline Commissioning Progress' chart dated 5 Oct 2026, '20-ID-D,E: HEXM XSD' is at stage 6, 'Restart of General User Program' (r13). The APS Proposal Types page (dated 10.07.2026) lists 20-ID-D,E among beamlines taking General User regular and rapid-access proposals (r16). How it got there, from the monthly charts (r13): Sep-Nov 2024, stage 1 (installation ongoing); Dec 2024-Jan 2025, stage 2 (installation complete); Mar 2025, stage 3 (ops commissioning); by Jul 2025 through Jan 2026, stage 5 (scientific commissioning and early experiments). In July 2025, Energy Secretary Chris Wright placed an 'inaugural sample', part of a jet-engine turbine blade, in the HEXM instrument (r14). A July 2025 NSUF/APS report says the beamline 'achieved shielding verification in 2025' and expected general users in late 2025 or early 2026 (r18). The first-light date was not published. The charts show stage 1 on 30 Sep 2024, stage 2 (installation complete) on 16 Dec 2024 and in Jan 2025, stage 3 (ops commissioning) on 10 Mar 2025 and stage 5 by July 2025 (r13). So first X-rays most likely reached the beamline between late January and July 2025, probably by March if stage 3 already involved beam-on shielding verification (not confirmed). The September 2024 update had expected HEXM first light in that run (r15); the charts show this did not happen in 2024. Caveats: (1) the Beamline Directory entry (read 2026-10-08) still says 'Current Status: Commissioning', and its specs assume a superconducting undulator. It warns they 'will not be fully valid during the startup of the beamline, which could last ~year' (r9). (2) The source is still an interim pair of permanent-magnet undulators: U21 upstream and a U21/U25 revolver downstream (ID table updated 22 Sep 2026, r12). The baseline in-line superconducting undulator pair (2 x 1.9 m, 16.5 mm period) was delayed by SCU core-reliability problems and is planned for 2026-2027 (r17). The Strategic Plan schedule (Fig. 8) shows 20-ID SCU core fabrication through 2026-2027 and commissioning around late 2027. It also targeted the first in-line SCU (sector 1) for May 2026, but the 22 Sep 2026 ID table still lists no SCU at sector 1 or 20, so the SCU schedule has slipped (r17, r12). (3) The adjacent Activated Materials Laboratory is operational. A Partner User Proposal gives NSUF 690 h/yr shared between 1-ID and 20-ID, starting in the 2025-3 run (r18, r19). HEXM was already absent from the August 2025 list of the 'last five feature beamlines' still to come online (r55).

tagline: A 180-meter X-ray microscope that looks deep inside metal parts and zooms from whole components down to atoms.
plainSummary: Ordinary X-rays are stopped by a fraction of a millimeter of steel. HEXM uses very high-energy X-rays, 35 to 120 thousand electron-volts, which pass through millimeters of metal (r1). So scientists can watch what happens inside a jet-engine alloy, a battery or a piece of reactor steel while it is pulled, heated or charged. The beamline is 180 meters long. Its main experiment room, 20-ID-E, had to be built in a separate building next to the APS ring, and it is the largest X-ray enclosure ever built at the APS (r21). The extra distance does two opposite jobs. It lets the beam spread out to several millimeters, so a whole sample can be seen at once, or be squeezed to a spot about 200 nanometers tall (about 430 nanometers wide) to zoom in on a single crystal grain (r8, r1, r20). Detectors from a few centimeters to about 16 meters behind the sample show how thousands of tiny crystals are oriented and strained, where cracks begin and how the spacing between atoms changes. Next door, a special laboratory lets researchers safely handle radioactive samples taken from nuclear reactors (r18).
expertSummary: HEXM (20-ID) is a single-branch, white-beam-capable APS-U feature beamline for bulk, in situ materials science at 35-120 keV, first proposed in a 2015 white paper (r31, r1, r9). Stations: optics enclosure 20-ID-A at about 26-36 m; white-beam station 20-ID-D at about 70 m on the experiment floor, home of the NSF-MRI high-throughput HEDM instrument; and the 19.8 m 20-ID-E in the Long Beamline Building, with the sample at about 180.7 m and detectors out to about 197 m (r1, r11, r28). Optics: white-beam diamond CRLs (L1); an LN2-cooled bent double-Laue Si(111) monochromator in nested inverse-Cauchois geometry, diffracting horizontally to preserve the 4 pm vertical emittance (25-35 mm outboard offset, dE/E about 1e-3; Cinel, installed 2024); an optional in-line (+--+) four-bounce monochromator (1e-4 with Si(111), 1e-5 to 1e-6 with high-order reflections) fed by collimating lenses; and refractive focusing and expanding optics at 28-33, 68-76 and 178.8 m. Beams range from 0.43 x 0.21 um FWHM (f = 2 m, 70 keV) to several mm (r1, r5, r11). One calibrated 20-ID-E sample position serves nf-, ff- and vff-HEDM, WAXS/PDF, scattering tomography, HE-SAXS (Qmin about 7e-4 /A at 40 keV), uCT, high-energy TXM and BCDI (48 x 31 um coherent focus, dE/E = 2e-6 at 40 keV). High-resolution and high-load sample manipulators and detector movers cover 2-theta up to 18 deg out to about 16 m (r1, r5, r28, r29). The source is still interim: in-line permanent-magnet U21 and U21/U25 revolver undulators, pending a 2 x 1.9 m, 16.5 mm-period SCU pair (r12, r17).

whatAPSUEnables.plain: The old APS made a broad, fuzzy X-ray source. The upgraded ring makes a source about 19 times narrower side-to-side, and its light is far more 'in step' (coherent), more like a laser pointer than a flashlight (r4). HEXM uses this in two opposite ways. Because the source is tiny, lenses 180 m away can still squeeze the beam into a spot only about 200 nanometers high (r1). The final lens can still sit about a meter upstream of the sample (the 'working distance', r8), which leaves room for heavy furnaces, load frames and battery cyclers. Because the beam stays narrow and parallel, it can also be spread into a smooth beam several millimeters wide, big enough to image a whole realistic sample at once (r20). And because more of the light is coherent, scientists can use 'lensless' coherent imaging to map the strain inside one crystal grain buried in a metal. Before the upgrade, only about 1 in 100,000 X-ray photons at these energies was coherent, too few for this to work (r7).
whatAPSUEnables.expert: The MBA lattice cuts the horizontal emittance from 3113 pm to 42 pm. In brightness (flat-beam) mode the vertical emittance is about 4 pm, compared with about 40 pm before (r4, r5, r35). At high photon energy the intrinsic radiation divergence is small (sigma_r' proportional to sqrt(lambda/L)), so the electron-beam size and divergence set the photon phase space in both planes. The vertical emittance reduction therefore pays off at 35-120 keV in a way it does not at low energy (r5, Table 6.21). A long beamline turns this into five things. (i) Strong demagnification at long working distances: 209 nm vertical FWHM at 180 m with an f = 2 m CRL at 70 keV, and 77 nm with an f = 1 m kinoform and 1.4e-4 bandwidth (r1, Table 4.30). (ii) Low-demagnification or magnifying geometries: L2+L5 vertically and L5 horizontally give a 48 x 31 um spot that can be apertured to near-full transverse coherence for BCDI on 10-20 um grains. The design projected about 500x the coherent flux and 150x the coherent fraction of pre-upgrade 1-ID at 40 keV (r1, r5). (iii) Efficient refractive beam expansion: about 480 um FWHM at 34 m becomes 3-4 mm at 180 m, for nf-HEDM line beams and uCT (r5). (iv) Narrow-acceptance high-resolution crystal optics pass more flux. (v) A 20 m end station allows sample-detector distances up to about 15-16 m for vff-HEDM and oversampling of BCDI fringes, a SAXS Qmin 6x below 1-ID-E, and TXM toward about 100 nm (r5).
quantitative: Horizontal emittance 3113 pm (pre-upgrade APS) -> 42 pm (APS-U brightness mode), about 74x smaller; horizontal rms source size 280 -> 14.7 um (r4)

Nominal ID-straight electron-beam parameters from the design-lattice model (flat-beam mode, zero current; computed values, not measurements): sigma_x = 14.5 um, sigma_x' = 2.75 urad, sigma_y = 3.08 um, sigma_y' = 1.29 urad (r35)
Coherent fraction at HEDM energies was about 1e-5 before the upgrade, too low for high-energy CDI (r7)
Projected gains at 40 keV vs pre-upgrade 1-ID: about 500x coherent flux and 150x coherent fraction (r5)
Smallest design focus at 20-ID-E: 0.43 x 0.21 um FWHM at 70 keV with 4e11 ph/s (f = 2 m, L6), with sub-100 nm vertical projected using an f = 1 m kinoform (r1)

Largest beams: unfocused 2.5 x 2.2 mm FWHM at 180 m (70 keV), or several mm via refractive expanders. Sample cross-sections 'were one millimeter before. Now they can be up to several millimeters' (Almer) (r1, r20)
SAXS: Qmin = 0.0007 /A at 40 keV (dmax about 870 nm), a 6x larger observable range than 1-ID-E (r5)
Scattering-tomography resolution set by beam size: about 2 um before, about 0.1 um planned (r6)
Planned SCU vs the pre-upgrade SCU1 at 1-ID: 530x brilliance, 4.5x central-cone flux, and 1.5x flux density even after moving from 70 m to 180 m (r5)
Expected data rates about 100x those of 1-ID before the upgrade (r5)

techniques.name: Far-field high-energy diffraction microscopy
techniques.plain: A metal is a jigsaw of thousands of tiny crystals (grains). Each grain throws back a few sharp X-ray spots. If you rotate the sample and track every spot, a computer can work out where each grain is, which way it points, and how much it is being stretched or squeezed.
techniques.expert: Box or line beam of about 1-2 mm through a polycrystal, with an omega rotation series of area-detector frames at about 0.5-1.5 m. Peaks are indexed per grain (MIDAS/HEXRD), giving center of mass, orientation and the full elastic strain tensor for up to about 10^4 grains. At 1-ID-E the measured repeatability was about 5 um in position, 0.02 deg in orientation and 2e-4 in strain (r41, r30). HEXM runs it at 20-ID-D (high-throughput instrument) and at 20-ID-E (detector D2/D3) (r10, r29). Review: r42.

techniques.name: Near-field high-energy diffraction microscopy
techniques.plain: A camera placed just a centimeter or two behind the sample records diffraction spots almost where they leave the grain. That is enough to draw a 3D map of the grains and their boundaries, like a CT scan colored by crystal orientation.
techniques.expert: Line-focus beam (sub-um vertically, ideally 3-4 mm horizontally) sliced through the sample. A high-resolution scintillator+objective detector (D1) records at several distances of 1-2 cm while the sample rotates and steps vertically. Forward modeling reconstructs 3D orientation maps at about 1 um and 0.01 deg resolution (r5). HEXM's long beamline lets the L3 diamond expanders make the wide line beam efficiently (r5).

techniques.name: Very-far-field HEDM
techniques.plain: Move the detector many meters away and each diffraction spot spreads out, so tiny changes in the spacing of atoms (strain) become visible, even inside a single grain.
techniques.expert: Detector at 10 m or more (D3/D4 in 20-ID-E, 2-16 m from the sample) for high reciprocal-space resolution; strain sensitivity scales as dd/d = -cot(theta) d(theta), so longer L gives a smaller angular pixel. It needs about 1e-4 bandwidth from the four-bounce monochromator (r1, r5, r28).

techniques.name: Wide-angle X-ray scattering / high-energy diffraction / pair distribution function
techniques.plain: Diffraction rings from many grains at once tell you which crystal phases are present and how hard each one is being loaded, much like weighing a crowd instead of each person.
techniques.expert: Phase fractions, lattice strains per hkl, texture, peak broadening (defect density) and PDF to high Q. Measured in transmission at 2-theta below about 10-18 deg. It works with monochromatic beam or with a focused full undulator harmonic (0.6% BW, 4.8e14 ph/s at 70 keV) for the highest flux (r1, r30). Diffracted-beam apertures (conical or spiral slits) can add depth resolution (r5).

techniques.name: Scattering tomography
techniques.plain: Scan a pencil-thin beam across a sample and rotate it, collecting diffraction at each step. A computer builds a 3D map of which material, and how much strain, sits at each point inside.
techniques.expert: Translate-rotate tomography with WAXS and/or SAXS contrast (absorption, diffraction phase, lattice parameter). Real-space resolution equals the beam size, so HEXM's focusing takes it from about 2 um toward about 0.1 um (r6, r30).

techniques.name: High-energy small-angle X-ray scattering
techniques.plain: X-rays scattered by very small angles reveal nanometer-scale holes, precipitates and fibers, things too small to see directly but very important for strength.
techniques.expert: SAXS detector (D6) about 14 m downstream with focusing and guard slits gives Qmin = 0.0007 /A at 40 keV (dmax about 870 nm). That range overlaps for the first time with direct-space TXM imaging of the same voids or particles (r5).

techniques.name: Micro-computed tomography (absorption and phase contrast)
techniques.plain: A 3D X-ray scan, like a hospital CT but with micrometer detail, showing pores, cracks and second phases inside dense parts.
techniques.expert: Full-field radiography and tomography; resolution is roughly beam size/1000 (r30). Expanded white or pink beams allow about 1 um-resolution datasets in fractions of a second (r5). Phase contrast benefits from the higher coherence (r6).

techniques.name: High-energy transmission X-ray microscopy
techniques.plain: A real X-ray lens after the sample magnifies its image onto a camera far away, like a slide projector, to see details much finer than a normal CT.
techniques.expert: Refractive objective (L7) after the sample imaging onto detector D5 about 15 m downstream. 1-ID demonstrated about 500 nm resolution at 45 keV within 6 m; the HEXM goal is about 100 nm with higher magnification and depth of field (r5, r50).

techniques.name: Bragg coherent diffraction imaging (high-energy)
techniques.plain: Shine a coherent (laser-like) beam on one buried crystal grain. Its diffraction spot becomes a speckled 3D pattern. A computer turns this pattern back into a 3D image of the grain's shape and of how its atoms are displaced, with detail of tens of nanometers.
techniques.expert: Coherent 48 x 31 um focus at 40 keV (3.8e9 ph/s, dE/E = 2e-6, from the high-order four-bounce monochromator) for grains up to about 10-20 um. Grains are targeted using the ff-HEDM orientation map; fringes are oversampled on detector D4 about 16 m away (r1, r5). Proof of principle at 1-ID-E at 52 keV used a collimating lens, the 1-ID high-resolution four-bounce monochromator (bandwidth not stated in the paper; the FDR describes the 1-ID unit as about 1e-4), a vertically focusing saw-tooth lens giving a 1.5 x 50 um beam, and an ASI Lynx 1800 (Medipix3, 55 um pixels) photon-counting detector 6.12 m from the sample. It imaged structures of 477 +/- 50 nm or smaller with about 2.5e-4 strain resolution, with grains selected by ff-HEDM (r40, r53, r56).

techniques.name: Dark-field X-ray microscopy
techniques.plain: Like TXM, but the lens is placed in a diffracted beam, so it images only one chosen grain and shows tiny tilts and strains inside it, like a microscope tuned to a single crystal.
techniques.expert: An objective lens in a single Bragg reflection ('TXM in diffracted beams', PDR ref. to Simons et al.) maps orientation and strain at sub-um resolution deep in bulk grains. HEXM has been described as 'the only beamline worldwide to offer dark-field X-ray microscopy at high energies' (A. Bucsek). This is a planned or emerging mode; no published HEXM DFXM result was found (r5, r44, r20).

scienceCases.title: Why turbine alloys crack: dwell fatigue in Ti and Ni superalloys
scienceCases.plain: Jet-engine parts fail after many cycles of stress with long holds at temperature. HEXM can watch thousands of grains inside a real alloy sample under load and heat, find the few 'hot spot' grains where strain piles up, then zoom in on them to see where a crack is about to start.
scienceCases.expert: nf-HEDM maps about 1000 grains, and ff-HEDM gives grain-averaged elastic strain tensors under in situ thermo-mechanical load (RAMS-type load frames). Selected grains then go to BCDI/DFXM for intragranular strain near boundaries, with TXM/uCT for void and crack nucleation. This tests the hypothesis that some slip systems are effectively in creep mode while others respond in a low-temperature mode, central to cold dwell (Ti alloys, even at room temperature) and hot dwell (Ni superalloys above about 700 C) (r6, r7, r43). The inaugural HEXM sample placed by Secretary Wright in July 2025 was part of a jet-engine turbine blade (r14).

scienceCases.title: Inside irradiated nuclear materials
scienceCases.plain: Steel and fuel from reactors become radioactive, so they are hard to study. The Activated Materials Laboratory next door to 20-ID-E prepares and seals such samples, and HEXM's penetrating X-rays then map cracks, voids and grain strains in 3D. The first user experiment looked at decades-old stainless-steel parts from a light-water reactor that had developed stress-corrosion microcracks.
scienceCases.expert: AML (DOE-NE/NSUF funded) accepts samples up to 100 mrem/h beta/gamma at 30 cm. NSUF has a Partner User Proposal for 690 h/yr split between 1-ID and 20-ID, starting in the 2025-3 run, and higher-dose samples are meant to go mainly to 20-ID because it sits outside the main hall (r18). Techniques are uCT, WAXS/SAXS and HEDM with in situ heating and loading (Psylotech uTS/xTS 5 kN, Linkam TS1500). The first AML user experiment (UIUC/ORNL/Alabama/ANL) examined grain-level correlates of IASCC in reactor-retired stainless steel. Which beamline it used was not stated (r19).

scienceCases.title: Additive manufacturing: pores, residual stress and grains in 3D-printed metal
scienceCases.plain: 3D-printed metal parts can hide tiny pores and locked-in stresses. HEXM can image the pores in large, realistic samples and measure the stress in each grain, even while the material is being made or welded.
scienceCases.expert: Large-field uCT with resolution down to about 100 nm finds small pores in statistically relevant volumes. HEDM and SAXS give grain orientations, residual strains and nano-precipitates. In operando processing is planned to narrow the processing parameter space, with real-time analysis feedback (r6, r8).

scienceCases.title: Batteries that crack as they charge
scienceCases.plain: Battery cathode particles are clumps of nano-crystals that crack apart after many charges. HEXM can look inside full-size cells to see where strain and cracks build up as they charge and discharge.
scienceCases.expert: Cathode secondary particles are made of 10-500 nm primary crystallites. Intergranular fracture is driven by anisotropic lattice changes during Li insertion. HEXM's nano-focused HEDM/BCDI aims at primary-particle-level stress fields in ensembles operating in bulk cells, and a Maccor 4300 cycler is listed in the station infrastructure (r6, r10, r8).

scienceCases.title: Bone and other natural composites
scienceCases.plain: Bone is built from protein fibers about 100 nanometers wide and mineral crystals. High-energy X-rays give a lower radiation dose and can map how strain is shared between these parts when bone is loaded.
scienceCases.expert: SAXS/WAXS scattering tomography with beam-size-limited resolution improved from about 2 um to about 0.1 um. Dose-optimal energies for biological tissue are about 60-100 keV, between the photoelectric- and Compton-dominated regimes (r6).

scienceCases.title: Grain mapping as a high-throughput service
scienceCases.plain: Built by four universities, the high-throughput HEDM instrument in 20-ID-D turns grain mapping into something like an assembly line, so many more samples can be measured, possibly even mailed in.
scienceCases.expert: NSF MRI consortium (CMU lead with Purdue, Utah and Colorado School of Mines; award 1726375). The instrument was first installed at 6-ID-D and moved to 20-ID-D in Dec 2023. It has a six-degree-of-freedom (Aerotech) sample manipulator. 'Many places with wading pools...this instrument...will be an Olympic swimming pool' (R. Suter) (r24, r25, r11, r18, r10).

keyParameters.label: Photon energy (monochromatic)
keyParameters.note: Beamline Directory gives 35-120 keV (r9). The 2021 D3 detector-mover spec quotes 35-140 keV for the photon delivery system (r28). White beam (and focused 'broadband' undulator harmonics) also available.

keyParameters.label: White-beam capability
keyParameters.note: Monochromators and lenses can be moved out of the beam for white-beam operation (r18).

keyParameters.label: Energy resolution dE/E
keyParameters.value: 1e-3 (bent double-Laue); about 1e-4 (four-bounce, Si(111)); 1e-5 to 1e-6 (four-bounce, high-order Si reflections)
keyParameters.note: AML report lists the optional high-resolution monochromator as dE/E of about 1e-5 (r18).

keyParameters.label: Flux, 70 keV unfocused at 20-ID-E
keyParameters.note: Design value assuming the 16.5 mm SCU. The current interim permanent-magnet source should give less: the Strategic Plan says SCUs boost brightness by about 3x over hybrid permanent-magnet undulators above 50 keV (r17). No measured 20-ID value is published.

keyParameters.label: Beam size range at sample
keyParameters.note: FDR: 0.43 x 0.21 um (f = 2 m, L6) to 2.5 x 2.2 mm unfocused (FDR Table 4.29 header says um, but the unfocused rows are mm; the Beamline Directory confirms mm) (r1, r9).

keyParameters.label: Working distance (focusing optic to sample)
keyParameters.note: FDR focal lengths 1-2 m for nano-focusing at 20-ID-E (r1).

keyParameters.label: BCDI coherent beam
keyParameters.value: 48 x 31 um FWHM, 3.8e9 ph/s at 40 keV, dE/E = 2e-6
keyParameters.note: Design configuration L2 (31 m) + L5 (76 m), FDR Fig. 4.20.

keyParameters.label: Broadband (pink) focused beam
keyParameters.value: 182 x 47 um (E) or 50 x 13 um (D), 4.8e14 ph/s, dE/E = 6e-3 at 70 keV
keyParameters.note: A full undulator harmonic focused by white-beam diamond lenses L1; 4-5x the monochromatic flux (r5).

keyParameters.label: Source-to-sample distances
keyParameters.note: The 20-ID-E sample origin is 3.5 m downstream of the upstream wall, which is about 177.5 m from the source (r28).

keyParameters.label: Beamline length to final stop
keyParameters.note: Often quoted as '180 m' (to the sample, r22) or '600-foot' (r8).

keyParameters.label: Diffraction-angle coverage
keyParameters.value: 2-theta up to 18 deg (1 A d-spacing at 40 keV) over 2-12 m (D3) and on the back wall (D4)

keyParameters.label: SAXS minimum Q
keyParameters.note: Design estimate with D6 at 14 m and 0.5 mm minimum radius.

keyParameters.label: Insertion devices (Sep 2026)
keyParameters.value: U21 (21 mm, 112 periods) + revolver U21/U25 in-line; Kmax 1.38 (U21); E1 = 8.36 keV
keyParameters.note: Interim. Baseline: 2 x 1.9 m, 16.5 mm-period NbTi SCU in one 4.8 m cryostat (r17, r3).

keyParameters.label: Monochromator M1
keyParameters.value: LN2-cooled bent double-Laue Si(111), horizontal deflection, 25-35 mm outboard fixed offset
keyParameters.note: Cinel, installed in 20-ID-A in Jan 2024 (r11); Si(111) per r9.

keyParameters.value: 19.8 m long; 6.8 m wide x about 4.0 m high (upstream 11.3 m), 10.8 m wide x 6.9 m high (downstream)
keyParameters.note: Beam height 1.4 m above floor. 'At roughly 20 meters, this will be the largest enclosure we've built at the APS' (r21).

keyParameters.label: 20-ID-E stability environment
keyParameters.note: HEXM enclosure floor slab 12 in thick (r23).

keyParameters.label: Front end
keyParameters.value: High-heat-load front end (21 kW, 590 kW/mrad^2 limits); 2 (H) x 1 (V) mm exit mask at 25.4 m; 5 x 5 mm exit collimator at 26.1 m

insertionDevices.name: APS21#5 (U21), upstream
insertionDevices.notes: 112 periods; device min gap 8.5 mm; Keff 1.38 at min gap; E1 = 8.36 keV (6.0 GeV, zero emittance); 216 kW/mrad^2 and 5.4 kW at 200 mA. Length = 112 x 21 mm (the Beamline Directory says '2.3 m length'). INTERIM source as of 22 Sep 2026.

insertionDevices.name: APS21R25#9 revolver (U21 / U25), downstream
insertionDevices.type: planar hybrid permanent-magnet revolver undulator (two magnetic structures, selectable)
insertionDevices.notes: Structure 1: APS21#14, 21 mm, 112 periods, K 1.38, E1 = 8.32 keV. Structure 2: APS25#11, 25 mm, 94 periods, K 1.98, E1 = 4.61 keV, 224 kW/mrad^2, 8.0 kW. The Beamline Directory lists the downstream source as U21. INTERIM source.

insertionDevices.name: SCU 16.5 mm in-line pair (baseline, not yet installed)
insertionDevices.type: planar superconducting undulator (NbTi), two magnets in one 4.8 m cryostat
insertionDevices.notes: APS-U baseline for sectors 1 and 20: 'two pairs of 1.9-meter-long, 16.5-mm period SCUs in inline configuration', with correctors inside the long cryostat. Installation was delayed by core reliability issues and is now planned for 2026-2027 (r17, r3, r49). FDR 4-4 (2019) specified about 3.5 m (possibly 3.8 m) total magnetic length, Kmax 1.63 (1.06 T at 8.0 mm gap), 1.6 kW and 600 kW/mrad^2 through the 2 x 1 mm mask. PDR: 17.9 kW total and 616 kW/mrad^2 at max field (r1, r5). A 2020 overview: 'Current undulator lengths are 1.1 m with up to 3.5m planned for the APS-Upgrade' (r46). The 2025-29 Strategic Plan schedule (Fig. 8) shows 20-ID SCU core fabrication through 2026-2027 and commissioning around late 2027. The plan's May 2026 target for the first in-line SCU (sector 1) had not been met by the 22 Sep 2026 ID table, which lists no SCU at sector 1 or 20 (r17, r12).

source.canting: none (two in-line devices on one straight; phase shifter/corrector between permanent-magnet devices; for the SCUs, correctors inside the cryostat)
source.frontEnd: Standard APS-U High-Heat-Load front end (HHLFE, based on the 28-ID design): total power limit 21 kW, peak power density 590 kW/mrad^2. Contents: clearing magnet, burn-through fixed mask (BTFM1), GRID XBPM1, photon shutter with intensity monitor, safety shutters, and exit mask with XBPM2 (r3). For 20-ID: window exit configuration with a 2 (H) x 1 (V) mm exit mask at 25.4 m and a 5 x 5 mm tungsten exit collimator at 26.1 m (r1, r3). The window material is inconsistent in the FDR: 0.5 mm Be in 4-4.3, diamond in Table 4.28.
source.sourceSizeAndDivergence: Electron beam at the ID straight (APS-U design-lattice model values at zero current, not measurements; r35). Flat-beam/brightness mode (kappa = 0.1): sigma_x = 14.47 um, sigma_x' = 2.75 urad, sigma_y = 3.08 um, sigma_y' = 1.29 urad. Round-beam/timing mode: sigma_x = 12.3 um, sigma_x' = 2.34 urad, sigma_y = 8.26 um, sigma_y' = 3.47 urad. FDR Table 1.1 design (brightness): 14.7 / 2.8 / 3.2 / 1.3 (r4). Computed here, not from a source: at 70 keV for a 2.35 m undulator the single-electron photon size and divergence are about 0.7 um and 1.9 urad. That gives total photon source sizes of about 14.5 x 3.2 um and divergences of about 3.4 x 2.3 urad rms, before energy-spread broadening, which becomes significant at the high harmonics (7th-13th) HEXM uses. FDR Fig. 4.20 uses 35 um (H) x 9 um (V) FWHM source sizes for the BCDI optics design, and the PDR text quotes the same 9 um vertical FWHM (r1, r5).

branches.name: 20-ID (single branch)
branches.description: One straight beamline with no net horizontal deflection. The bent Laue monochromator displaces the monochromatic beam about 25-35 mm outboard, parallel to the white-beam axis (r1). White or monochromatic beam goes to 20-ID-D (about 70 m) or, through a movable stop, on to 20-ID-E (about 180 m) in the Long Beamline Building (r5, r10).

components.name: Upstream undulator U21 (APS21#5)
components.distanceNote: approx: two 2.35 m devices in-line on the straight centered on the source point (0 m); device centers estimated at about +/-1.3 m
components.plain: A row of 224 alternating magnets (112 periods) makes the electrons wiggle, and each wiggle adds to a bright beam of X-rays. HEXM uses the very high-energy 'overtones' (harmonics) of this light.
components.expert: Hybrid PM, 21 mm period, 112 periods, Keff 1.38 at 8.5 mm min gap, E1 = 8.36 keV. 35 keV is reached on the 3rd harmonic, 70 keV on about the 7th (K about 1.1), 120 keV on the 11th-13th. 5.4 kW and 216 kW/mrad^2 at 200 mA. Interim device until SCUs arrive.

components.name: Downstream revolver undulator U21/U25 (APS21R25#9)
components.plain: A second undulator in line with the first doubles the light. It is a 'revolver': it carries two magnet rows and can rotate to pick a 21 mm or 25 mm magnet spacing.
components.expert: Revolver with APS21#14 (21 mm, 112 periods, K 1.38) and APS25#11 (25 mm, 94 periods, K 1.98, E1 = 4.61 keV). The Directory lists U21 as the downstream source. Phase shifter/corrector between the in-line pair. Baseline replacement: 2 x 1.9 m, 16.5 mm NbTi SCU in a 4.8 m cryostat (r17). IPAC'24: 'The SCUs are planned to be installed later' (r34).

components.name: High-heat-load front end (shutters, masks, XBPMs)
components.distanceNote: schematic placement inside the storage-ring tunnel; the front end ends at the ratchet wall at about 25.4-26.1 m (exact internal positions not published)
components.plain: The safety gate between the accelerator and the beamline. It catches unwanted power, measures where the beam points, and can shut the X-rays off in a fraction of a second.
components.expert: APS-U HHLFE: 21 kW / 590 kW/mrad^2 limits. Clearing magnet, BTFM1, GRID XBPM1, photon shutter with IM1, safety shutters SS1/SS2, exit mask with XBPM2. Two in-line U21 at min gap deliver about 10.8 kW total (sum of ID-table values).

components.name: Front-end exit mask and window
components.plain: A small 2 x 1 mm opening lets only the central, useful part of the X-ray cone through, and a thin window separates the accelerator vacuum from the beamline.
components.expert: 2 (H) x 1 (V) mm^2 exit aperture (narrower than the standard 2 x 2 mm) to limit heat load. Window: 0.5 mm Be per FDR 4-4.3/Table 4.27 note, but 'Diamond Window' in Table 4.28 (as-built unconfirmed).

components.name: Front-end exit collimator
components.plain: A heavy tungsten block with a small hole that stops stray high-energy radiation (bremsstrahlung) from the accelerator.
components.expert: HHL front-end exit collimator, 5 x 5 mm^2 aperture (tungsten).

components.name: White-beam filters F1 (20ID-FL-1)
components.plain: Thin sheets of diamond and silicon soak up the low-energy X-rays that would only heat the optics, letting the high-energy ones through.
components.expert: Diamond and Si filter sequence sharing a tank and stand (SP-1) with L1. Under 1 x 1 mm beams, less than 100 W per element and more than 85% total transmission at 40 keV. With S1 at 0.6 x 0.6 mm they hold the load on a 2.5 mm Si M1 crystal to 55-60 W or less for LN2 cooling.

components.name: High-heat-load white-beam slits S1 (20ID-SL-1)
components.plain: Water-cooled metal jaws trim the beam to just the bright central cone, about half a millimeter square.
components.expert: HHL variable-aperture photon absorber with tungsten edge inserts (design A300-SL0200). Max aperture 2 x 2 mm. Routine operation at 0.6 x 0.6 mm or smaller, enough to pass the full 70 keV central cone broadened by energy spread.

components.name: L1 white-beam diamond refractive lenses
components.plain: Stacks of tiny diamond lenses act on the unfiltered beam before any crystal picks a single color. Because a lens focuses each color at a slightly different distance, they bring one undulator harmonic (a slice about 0.6% wide in energy, the 'pink' beam) to a focus, giving 4-5 times more X-rays than the monochromatic beam. Other lens sets can instead spread the beam out for imaging.
components.expert: Cooled single-crystal diamond CRLs for broadband focusing of a full harmonic (0.6% BW): 182 x 47 um at E or 50 x 13 um at D with 4.8e14 ph/s at 70 keV. Alternatively, white-beam expansion to several mm for imaging. Manual element changes. R&D outside APS-U scope.

components.name: M1 high-energy bent double-Laue monochromator (20ID-MN-1)
components.plain: Two thin, bent silicon crystals pick out one X-ray color (energy). X-rays pass through the crystals rather than bouncing off them. Bending the crystals collects about ten times more X-rays than flat crystals would.
components.expert: Two cryogenically cooled (LN2) bent Si(111) Laue crystals in nested inverse-Cauchois (sequential Rowland) geometry. Rowland diameter about 30 m. The second crystal compensates the phase-space distortion of the first. Diffracting in the horizontal plane preserves the 4 pm vertical emittance. Fixed exit offset 25-35 mm outboard; tunable 35-120 keV; dE/E about 1e-3. Built-in white-beam stop after crystal 1. Si(111) Bragg angle about 1.6 deg at 70 keV (computed). The 1-ID predecessor gave more than 10x the flux of flat crystals. The Cinel unit was installed in 20-ID-A in Jan 2024 (r11); a March 2024 photo shows staff working on it (r47). The 1-ID predecessor design is described in r36.

components.name: Diamond window (20ID-WN-1)
components.plain: A thin diamond sheet seals off the monochromator's vacuum section while letting X-rays through almost untouched.
components.expert: Ends vacuum section 1 (front end window through M1).

components.name: L2 collimating lenses
components.plain: Weak lenses make the beam almost perfectly parallel so the next, very picky crystal can accept more of it.
components.expert: Vertical collimation (f about 31 m in the BCDI configuration) into the narrow Darwin width of M2. Shastri & Antipov (2026) report diamond collimating lenses placed after a high-heat-load monochromator to raise throughput into a narrow-acceptance high-resolution monochromator, followed by focusing for coherent diffraction 'on a long beamline' (abstract; presumably 20-ID, full text not retrieved) (r39; earlier diamond CRL tests r54).

components.name: M2 high-resolution four-bounce monochromator (20ID-MN-2)
components.plain: Four flat crystal reflections in a row narrow the X-ray color 10 to 1000 times further, needed to measure tiny strains and for coherent imaging.
components.expert: Optional in-line (+--+) dispersive four-reflection Si system, vertical diffraction, no net offset, in air. Si(111): dE/E about 1e-4 (vff-HEDM). High-order (444)-(660) reflections: 1e-5 to 1e-6 (BCDI on about 10 um grains). Crystal pairs on weak-link flexures; apertures after the 2nd and 4th reflections. It follows the 1-ID flat-crystal/bent-crystal/CRL combination (r37).

components.name: Attenuators F2 and calibration foils F3
components.distanceNote: approx from FDR Fig. 4.19 (between M2 and L3; not in Table 4.28)
components.plain: Rotating wheels slide metal sheets into the beam, either to dim it or to check its exact energy against known absorption edges.
components.expert: Wheel-actuated monochromatic attenuators (flux control) and elemental foils (energy calibration and drift monitoring); designs proven at 1-ID.

components.name: Monochromatic slits S2
components.distanceNote: approx: drawn between foils F3 and lenses L3 in FDR Fig. 4.19; not listed in FDR Table 4.28
components.plain: Adjustable jaws that trim the single-color beam before the last lenses in the optics hutch.
components.expert: One of the monochromatic slit sets (S2-S6, S8) on stage stacks with manual or motorized rotations for one-time alignment to the beam (FDR 4-4.6.4).

components.name: L3 long-focal-length focusing / beam-expanding lenses
components.distanceNote: exact (FDR Table 4.28; 'not in project scope'); PDR quotes about 34 m
components.plain: Lenses that can either gently focus the beam into the far stations or spread it out into a wide, flat beam several millimeters across.
components.expert: Monochromatic focusing to 155 x 40 um at E or 39 x 10 um at D (70 keV, 8e13 ph/s). Convex or concave diamond expanders turn about 480 um FWHM (H) into 3-4 mm at 180 m for nf-HEDM and uCT. Can define a secondary source for L6. Shastri & Antipov (2026) propose convex diamond beam expanders for high-energy X-rays from a low-emittance source on a long beamline and report a proof-of-principle test (abstract, r39). The lens position and parameters they used were not verified (full text not retrieved).

components.name: Be window, photon mask and tungsten collimator (20ID-WN-2, PM-1, BC-1)
components.plain: Radiation-safety hardware that keeps the beam inside its pipe and blocks stray high-energy radiation.
components.expert: Collimator/mask pairs ratchet down the bremsstrahlung cone along the line of sight (white-beam operation gives a direct line of sight to the source).

components.name: White-beam / bremsstrahlung shutter (P4-80)
components.plain: The main door for the beam: when closed, people can safely enter the experiment stations downstream.
components.expert: Multi-mode WB/bremsstrahlung shutter (white or monochromatic mode) at the downstream end of the optics enclosure.

components.name: Shielded white-beam transport ST-1 (through legacy 20-ID-B/C)
components.plain: A lead-shielded pipe carries the beam about 30 m across the hall, straight through two older hutches that are no longer used.
components.expert: White-beam-capable evacuated shielded transport. The legacy 20-ID-B and 20-ID-C (mono) end stations 'will remain but not be used for operations' (r11).

components.name: 20-ID-D entrance: mask, collimator, Be window (PM-2, BC-2)
components.plain: More safety blocks and a window where the beam enters the first experiment hutch.
components.expert: Photon mask 66.2 m, tungsten collimator 66.5 m, Be window 66.8 m.

components.name: Multi-beam slits S3 (20ID-SL-3)
components.plain: Adjustable jaws that shape the beam. They can also make a tiny 'virtual source' for sharper focusing.
components.expert: Motorized for remote use as secondary-source apertures for focal-spot stability and transverse-coherence tuning.

components.name: Fast shutter (20ID-FS-1)
components.plain: A fast shutter, like a camera's, that times each X-ray exposure exactly.
components.expert: Compact fast shutter controlling detector exposure.

components.name: L4 short-focal-length focusing optics
components.plain: Strong lenses that squeeze the beam to about a micrometer for experiments in 20-ID-D.
components.expert: f below 2 m (saw-tooth, kinoform or CRL): 0.96 x 0.87 um, 2.7e12 ph/s at 70 keV (brightness mode). Four stage stacks for 2D saw-tooth focusing. Candidates: Si saw-tooth lenses, which are continuously tunable (r38), and kinoforms, which reached 230 nm FWHM at 51 keV and 660 nm at 102 keV at 1-ID (r51, r5).

components.name: Multi-beam slits S4 (20ID-SL-4)
components.plain: Clean-up slits just before the sample.
components.expert: Motorized guard or defining slits, also usable for coherence tuning.

components.name: High-throughput HEDM instrument (20-ID-D)
components.plain: A university-built grain-mapping machine that swaps and measures many samples quickly, like an assembly line for 3D crystal maps.
components.expert: Built by an NSF MRI consortium (CMU, Purdue, Utah, Colorado School of Mines; award 1726375). First installed at 6-ID-D, moved to 20-ID-D in Dec 2023. Six-DOF (Aerotech) sample manipulation; white-beam station also used for 'in-situ dynamics' and as optics delivery for 20-ID-E.

components.name: 20-ID-D area detector(s)
components.plain: A large flat X-ray camera that records the diffraction spots from the grains.
components.expert: FDR: 'Dexela 2923 or equivalent' CMOS flat panel. The Beamline Directory lists Varex 4343 and SpectrumLogic 3131HS area detectors for 20-ID (station assignment not stated).

components.name: Multi-beam slits S5 (20ID-SL-5)
components.plain: Aperture that selects the part of the beam sent on toward the far station.
components.expert: Defines the transversely coherent part of the beam for the L5 BCDI focusing configuration.

components.name: L5 long-focal-length lenses (focus into 20-ID-E)
components.plain: Gentle lenses that aim a focus about 100 m away, into the far experiment room. Used to make a wide, laser-like beam for coherent imaging.
components.expert: About 1:1 imaging into E: V f = 104 m (with L2), H f = 44 m. Gives 48 x 31 um at 40 keV for BCDI, or 48 x 13 um and 6.5e13 ph/s at 70 keV.

components.name: Movable white/bremsstrahlung beam stop (20ID-BS-1)
components.plain: A movable stop: closed, it ends the beam in 20-ID-D so people can work in 20-ID-E; open, it lets the beam travel on to the far station.
components.expert: Cooled movable stop for white and monochromatic beam; permits experiments in D with personnel access to E.

components.name: Long shielded transport ST-2 (hall to Long Beamline Building)
components.enclosure: transport (LOM 436 and the HEXM corridor of the LBB)
components.plain: A 100 m vacuum pipe, shielded with lead, leaves the APS hall, passes through the lab-office building and a new corridor lined with offices, and enters the Long Beamline Building. People cross it on stairs and an elevator.
components.expert: White-beam evacuated shielded transport, about 100 m. With ST-1 this adds up to the poster's 'White Beam Shielded Transport ~140 meters' (r29). Windows WN-3 at 77.0 m and WN-4 at 177.7 m in shielded boxes. MEDSI'18 vacuum analysis for the ISN long transport (146 m, 4 in ID) used 4 x 200 L/s pumps (r32).

components.name: 20-ID-E entrance window and white-beam slits (WN-4, SL-7)
components.plain: Where the beam arrives in the giant end station, slits trim it again.
components.expert: Portable end-station white-beam slits (S7) handle the high power density near broadband foci.

components.name: Beam-conditioning optics table with L6 nano-focusing lenses
components.distanceNote: exact for L6 (FDR Table 4.28); table spans about 178-180 m (approx)
components.plain: A long, stable table holds the final lenses, slits and beam monitors. The lenses can squeeze the X-rays to a spot about 200 nanometers high.
components.expert: BCS table: L6 (f below 2 m) gives 0.43 x 0.21 um and 4e11 ph/s at 70 keV. Spot budget (f = 2 m, 150 um aperture, dE/E 1e-3): 99 nm demag (+) 152 nm chromatic (+) 104 nm diffraction = 209 nm V. With an f = 1 m, 400 um kinoform and dE/E 1.4e-4: 77 nm. Also slits S6/S8, ion chambers (some position-sensitive) and a fast shutter.

components.name: Be window 20ID-WN-5 (temporary)
components.plain: A thin beryllium window where the evacuated beam path ends just before the sample, so the X-rays travel the last stretch in air.
components.expert: Listed as a temporary Be window 0.7 m upstream of the sample position. The PDR describes optional evacuated flight tubes with an extra cooled window to remove air gaps, especially for white beam.

components.name: Sample position: HR-SMS, HL-SMS and RAMS load frame
components.distanceNote: exact (FDR Table 4.28: 20ID-BI-3); ESD-010 places the origin 3.5 m from the upstream wall, 1.4 m above floor
components.plain: One fixed spot where all the techniques meet. Precision stages or a heavy-duty platform hold the sample, and loading rigs stretch, heat or cycle it while the X-rays look inside.
components.expert: Single calibrated sample position shared by all detectors. High-Resolution SMS (hexapod with a rotation stage, per the poster rendering; bearing type not stated) and High-Load SMS (wheeled cart with guide columns for load frames) are swapped via floor rails, under an overhead support structure. RAMS (rotational and axial motion load frame), Psylotech uTS/xTS, Linkam TS1500, Ambrell RF furnace, Maccor 4300 cycler. PDR planned 2-4 SMSs for deformation, AM and electrochemistry.

components.name: D1 near-field / imaging detector
components.distanceNote: approx: 1-2 cm behind the sample for nf-HEDM (PDR); further downstream for uCT
components.plain: A high-resolution camera almost touching the sample: a thin scintillator turns X-rays into visible light, which a microscope lens records.
components.expert: LuAG:Ce thin-scintillator plus mirror plus microscope objective, about 1 um resolution. High-energy efficiency is low (less than 10% stopping above 40 keV), hence R&D. Used for nf-HEDM and uCT.

components.name: D2 detector system (near far-field WAXS/HEDM)
components.distanceNote: approx: about 1 m behind the sample (inferred from the PDR concept and poster rendering)
components.plain: A large flat-panel camera on a robotic platform that catches the diffraction rings close to the sample.
components.expert: Hexapod-mounted detector platform (poster). PDR concept: Dexela 2923 / GE-41RT-class flat panels for WAXS and ff-HEDM.

components.name: L7 TXM objective (direct or diffracted beam)
components.distanceNote: approx: PDR places L7 'after the sample'; the poster shows a TXM objective stand in the downstream hutch; exact distance unpublished
components.plain: An X-ray lens after the sample acts as a microscope objective, projecting a magnified image of the sample, or of one glowing grain, onto a camera at the back of the room.
components.expert: Refractive TXM objective in the direct beam (TXM, about 100 nm goal) or in a diffracted beam (DFXM-type). It can also relay far-field patterns for vff-HEDM and BCDI.

components.name: D3 detector manipulation system (2-12 m WAXS / HEDM)
components.distanceNote: exact range Z = 183-193 m (ESD-010); FDR Table 4.28: 183.3-192.5 m
components.plain: A detector on a tall moving tower that travels about 10 m along the floor rails and several meters sideways and up, to catch diffraction anywhere in a cone 36 degrees wide.
components.expert: Covers the 2-theta of 18 deg or less cone (1 A at 40 keV) at 2-12 m. Travel of at least 5 m in X, 3.5 m in Y and 9.5 m in Z, plus tilts of -20/+10 deg and +/-20 deg. Repeatability 75 um or better; 15 um or better per 24 h; 100 kg detector (reference: Pilatus3 X CdTe 6M, 172 um). Parks clear of SAXS/TXM/D4. A laser tracker monitors position. The FDR's robot-arm concept became a floor-rail tower (poster).

components.name: D6 SAXS detector
components.distanceNote: approx: about 14 m from the sample (PDR); SAXS table near the back wall in ESD Fig. 2
components.plain: A camera far behind the sample that catches X-rays scattered by only tiny angles, revealing nano-sized pores and particles.
components.expert: Qmin 0.0007 /A at 40 keV. PDR concept: Pixirad-class photon-counting detector.

components.name: D5 TXM imaging detector
components.distanceNote: approx: about 15 m from the sample (PDR)
components.plain: The 'projection screen' camera for the X-ray microscope.
components.expert: High-resolution, high-efficiency imaging detector. KA Imaging reports BrillianSe amorphous-selenium direct-conversion detectors (8 um pixels) 'designed into' the new 20-ID (vendor statement, r45). The vendor does not say which detector position it serves; assigning it to D5 here is an inference.

components.name: D4 back-wall detector system (BCDI / vff-HEDM)
components.plain: A detector that moves across the far wall, about 16 m from the sample, catching the finest speckle patterns and the tiniest changes in diffraction angle.
components.expert: Upper half-cone of 2-theta up to 17.8 deg (1 A at 40 keV) reaches the back wall. Friedel pairs accessible. Needs 5 um or better resolution with high efficiency and dynamic range for oversampling BCDI fringes (R&D). Separate spec ESD-011.

components.name: Fixed white-beam stop (20ID-BS-2)
components.plain: The end of the line: a cooled block that safely absorbs whatever is left of the beam.
components.expert: Cooled fixed stop for white and monochromatic beam at the downstream wall.

enclosures.name: Storage-ring tunnel / front end
enclosures.role: accelerator tunnel: in-line undulators and HHL front end through the ratchet wall
enclosures.notes: Start is approximate (straight-section length); front-end exit mask at 25.4 m (r1).

enclosures.name: 20-ID-A
enclosures.role: first optics enclosure (white-beam filters/slits, L1-L3 lenses, M1, M2, shutter)
enclosures.notes: Extent measured from FDR Fig. 4.18 (scale from the 19.8 m E-station), about +/-0.5 m; components 26.5-35.0 m (r1, r11).

enclosures.name: Shielded transport ST-1
enclosures.role: white-beam shielded transport in the experiment hall

enclosures.name: 20-ID-B (legacy, unused)
enclosures.role: former spectroscopy hutch; beam passes through in shielded pipe
enclosures.notes: Measured from FDR Fig. 4.18 (approx); 'will remain but not be used for operations' (r11).

enclosures.name: 20-ID-C (legacy, unused)
enclosures.role: former spectroscopy hutch; beam passes through in shielded pipe

enclosures.name: 20-ID-D
enclosures.role: white-beam experimental station on the main floor (high-throughput HEDM, in situ dynamics, optics for E)
enclosures.notes: New enclosure (red 'new work' in FDR Fig. 4.18). About 5 m wide upstream, with the outboard wall tapering toward the downstream end (2019 drawing; approx) (r1, r9).

enclosures.name: Shielded transport ST-2 and HEXM corridor
enclosures.role: about 100 m transport out of the hall, through LOM Bldg 436, along a new corridor with 14 offices into the Long Beamline Building
enclosures.notes: Corridor width about 5.6 m from site analysis (site.json); offices and building changes per r23, r2.

enclosures.name: 20-ID-E
enclosures.role: main experimental station in the Long Beamline Building (Bldg 444); lead-shielded, multi-modal
enclosures.notes: Interior 19.8 m long. Upstream section 11.3 m long x 6.8 m wide x about 4.0 m to the crane runway/roof (roof walkway on top). Downstream section 8.5 m x 10.8 m wide x 6.9 m high. Beam 1.4 m above floor, 5.4 m from the outboard wall in the wide section. Doorways on both sides at about 185 m (r28). Floor slab 12 in (r23). A yellow bridge crane with chain hoist spans the tall downstream section (r11 panorama photo, Jan 2024); ESD Fig. 2 marks a crane-runway level at the top of the low upstream section (r28). The LBB exists to give long-distance optics, low-background environments and better stability (r33).

enclosures.name: Activated Materials Laboratory (AML)
enclosures.role: radiological sample-prep lab adjacent to 20-ID-E (not on beam axis)
enclosures.notes: On the inboard side of 20-ID-E (FDR Fig. 4.1; LBB photo shows AML-HEXM-ISN in that order); funded by DOE-NE NSUF (r2, r17, r18).

enclosures.name: 20-ID-E control room and sample-prep area
enclosures.notes: On the outboard side, between HEXM and ISN, in the 2019 plan (FDR Fig. 4.1; approx); as-built layout not verified (r2).

instruments.name: High-Throughput HEDM instrument (HT-HEDM)
instruments.plain: An 'assembly-line' grain-mapping station built by four universities, moved to HEXM in December 2023.
instruments.expert: NSF MRI award 1726375 (CMU lead; Purdue, Utah, Colorado School of Mines; $1.09 M obligated). Six-DOF Aerotech sample manipulator; white beam or monochromatic; ff-HEDM, WAXS, imaging; high-throughput and potential mail-in operation.
detectors: Varex 4343 / SpectrumLogic 3131HS (Beamline Directory; station not specified)

instruments.name: 20-ID-E multi-modal end-station instrument
instruments.plain: A room-sized X-ray microscope: one sample spot, two sample stages, and a set of cameras from a few centimeters to 16 meters away. Users can switch between 3D grain maps, CT scans, nano-scale scattering and coherent imaging without moving the sample.
instruments.expert: Beam-conditioning optics table (L6, slits, ion chambers, fast shutter). HR-SMS (hexapod plus rotation stage) and HL-SMS (high-load cart with load-frame columns) on floor rails under an overhead support truss; RAMS load frame. Detector systems: D1 (nf/imaging), D2 (hexapod-mounted, near ff), D3 (2-12 m tower, 2-theta up to 18 deg), D4 (back wall, about 197 m), D5 (TXM), D6 (SAXS, about 14 m). TXM objective L7. Laser-tracker metrology (Leica AT9xx class). Stability: +/-0.05 C per 24 h, VC-E floor. The 20-ID-D and 20-ID-E instruments were presented at the Oct 2021 HEXM town hall (A. Chuang, J.-S. Park) (r48).
detectors: D3 large-area detector on DMS (Pilatus3 X CdTe 6M used as the spec reference)
KA Imaging BrillianSe a-Se (8 um pixel; vendor claim 'designed into' 20-ID; position not stated)
sampleEnvironments: RAMS rotational and axial motion load frame
Psylotech uTS / xTS 5 kN load frames (AML)

instruments.name: Activated Materials Laboratory (support facility)
instruments.plain: A safe workshop for radioactive samples, with glove boxes and shielded containers, right next to the X-ray hutch.
instruments.expert: DOE-NE NSUF-funded radiological facility. Fume hoods, shielded glove boxes, encapsulation, transport to 1-ID and 20-ID. Sample limit 100 mrem/h at 30 cm. NSUF Partner User Proposal of 690 h/yr.

geometryNotes: Single straight line from the 20-ID straight section to the fixed stop at 197 m, with no net horizontal deflection. The bent double-Laue M1 (29.5 m) displaces the monochromatic beam 25-35 mm outboard and parallel; white-beam operation runs on axis. The four-bounce M2 has zero net offset (r1). The beam is tangent to the ring at sector 20, so the line leaves the hall at a slight angle to its neighbors. The ISN (19-ID) line starts about 2 m inboard but is rotated 9 deg outboard, so in the Long Beamline Building ISN lies on HEXM's outboard side. Outboard means the left of the beam direction, APS +X (r28; site.json gives a 20-ID direction of 168.8 deg vs 177.8 deg for 19-ID in site coordinates). Inside the hall: 20-ID-A against the ratchet wall (about 26-36 m), a shielded pipe through the unused legacy 20-ID-B and -C hutches (about 50-65 m), then the new 20-ID-D (about 65-77 m) as far downstream as the hall allows. The about 100 m ST-2 pipe crosses the experiment-floor walkway (stairs and an elevator lift people over it, r15), passes through LOM Bldg 436, where offices were removed, and runs along a new office corridor into Bldg 444, the LBB (r23). 20-ID-E is a two-level lead hutch. The upstream third is low: 6.8 m wide, about 4 m high, with a roof walkway. The downstream part, from about 188.8 m, is wide and tall (10.8 x 6.9 m), so the 2-theta = 17.8 deg Debye cone (1 A at 40 keV) can reach the back-wall D4 detector about 16 m from the sample. Check: tan(17.8 deg) x 16.4 m = 5.3 m, against 5.4 m to the side walls and 5.5 m from beam height to the ceiling (r28, r29). Beam height 1.4 m. On the as-built poster an overhead truss bridges the sample area; D3 and D4 are tall tan pillar-type movers labeled 'HEXM'. The AML is on the inboard side of 20-ID-E. The control room and sample prep were drawn on the outboard side in 2019 (r2). Outside, the LBB massing reads AML (low) - HEXM (tall) - ISN (r17 photo). Caution for modelers: the FDR Fig. 4.1 caption says the beam travels left to right, but in that drawing the APS ring is at the right and the LBB at the left, so the beam actually runs right to left. Read that way, HEXM (top) is inboard of ISN (bottom) and the AML is inboard of HEXM, consistent with FDR Fig. 4.18 (beam left to right: control room and sample prep drawn above, i.e. outboard; AML below, i.e. inboard) (r2, r1).

interactiveIdeas.title: Zoom-in, zoom-out
interactiveIdeas.concept: Start with a jet-engine turbine blade, then scroll through powers of ten. At each step the exhibit switches technique and detector distance on the 3D hutch model: uCT (mm, beam size/1000), nf-HEDM grain map (um), ff-HEDM strain per grain, BCDI or DFXM inside one grain (tens of nm), and WAXS/PDF d-spacings (sub-A).
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: No single image covers 7 orders of magnitude. HEXM combines techniques at one sample position so each scale guides where to zoom next.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Direct imaging resolution is roughly beam size/1000. Grain-resolved HEDM works for up to about 1e4 grains in the beam. nf-HEDM resolves about 1 um and 0.01 deg. ff-HEDM gives about 2e-4 strain per grain. BCDI resolves tens of nm with strain about 1e-4. Keep 2-theta under about 10-18 deg at 35-120 keV (r30, r41, r5).

interactiveIdeas.title: X-ray vision vs energy
interactiveIdeas.concept: Slider from 10 to 120 keV with slabs of Al, Ti, steel, Ni superalloy, W. Show the transmitted beam and a 'see-through depth' gauge, and overlay a turbine blade, a battery and a reactor fuel pellet.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: Why HEXM needs high energy: the X-rays have to pass through real-size metal parts and their containment.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Use NIST mass attenuation coefficients (r52): I/I0 = exp(-(mu/rho) rho t). Fe 1/e length is about 7 um at 10 keV, 0.35 mm at 40 keV, about 1.5 mm at 70 keV and 3.4 mm at 100 keV. W and U stay strongly absorbing: the AML report puts their penetration near 100 um at 70 keV and above (r18). Computed NIST values span roughly 0.03-0.25 mm over 40-120 keV, with jumps at the W (69.5 keV) and U (115.6 keV) K edges. Show the W K-edge (69.5 keV) jump. Attenuation is not linear in E.

interactiveIdeas.title: Why 180 meters? Build your own focus
interactiveIdeas.concept: Drag a lens along the beam (D station at 70 m, E station at 180 m) and choose f. Live readout of the spot size as source demag (+) chromatic aberration (+) diffraction limit, and a toggle between brightness and timing source modes. A second mode turns the lens into a beam expander.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: Distance helps both ways: smaller spots at a convenient working distance, and wide, uniform beams for whole-sample imaging.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Thin lens 1/f = 1/p + 1/q; demagnified size = 2.355 sigma_source x q/p. FWHM terms add in quadrature: at 180 m, f = 2 m, 70 keV, 99 + 152 + 104 nm gives 209 nm (V, FDR Table 4.30). CRL focal length f = R/(2N delta); for diamond at 70 keV delta is about 1.5e-7 (computed from electron density), so R = 50 um needs N of about 84 for f = 2 m. Focal length scales as E^2 (delta proportional to lambda^2), so chromatic blur scales with dE/E. Kinoforms beat CRLs on aperture (r1, r5).

interactiveIdeas.title: Move the detector: near, far, very far
interactiveIdeas.concept: One polycrystal and one rotating sample. Slide the detector from 1 cm (nf) to 1 m (ff) to 15 m (vff). Spots spread out, position information fades and strain resolution sharpens. Then apply load and watch individual spots shift.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: The same diffraction carries different information depending on distance, and HEXM's 20 m hutch makes the 'very far' mode possible.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Bragg's law: lambda = 2 d sin(theta), lambda[A] = 12.398/E[keV]. Fe(110) at 70 keV has 2-theta of about 5.0 deg. Strain dd/d = -cot(theta) d(theta), and angular resolution is about pixel/L. Near field (1-2 cm) gives spatial maps; far field gives grain averages (r5, r41).

interactiveIdeas.title: Coherence and the speckle pattern of one grain (BCDI)
interactiveIdeas.concept: Compare old APS and APS-U source sizes. Show the coherence patch at 180 m, then illuminate one grain and show its 3D speckle. A detector-pixel slider reveals when fringes become undersampled, and a bandwidth slider shows fringes washing out unless dE/E is 1e-5 or below.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: Coherent imaging at high energy needed the upgrade, a very monochromatic beam and a very long hutch.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Gaussian Schell model: rms transverse coherence length xi = lambda z/(2 pi sigma). At 40 keV, 180 m, xi_x is about 60 um (APS-U, sigma_x 14.5 um) vs about 3 um (old APS, 280 um); this is computed, and conventions differ by factors of about 2. Longitudinal coherence is about lambda/(2 dE/E); at 40 keV (lambda = 0.31 A) that is about 15 nm at 1e-3, 1.5 um at 1e-5 and 7.8 um at 2e-6 (computed; some authors use lambda^2/dlambda, twice as long). Fringe period on the detector is lambda L/D, about 50 um for D = 10 um, L = 16 m at 40 keV, so pixels need to be 25 um or less. Design coherent focus is 48 x 31 um (FDR Fig. 4.20) (r1, r5, r35).

interactiveIdeas.title: Undulator harmonic ladder
interactiveIdeas.concept: Pick the current U21 or the future 16.5 mm SCU and drag K (the gap or current). Odd harmonics slide across 35-120 keV, and a meter shows how many harmonics overlap a chosen energy and how bright each is.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: High-energy beamlines run on high undulator harmonics. Shorter periods and stronger fields (superconducting magnets) put more photons where HEXM works.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: E_n[keV] = n x 0.9496 E_e[GeV]^2 / (lambda_u[cm] (1 + K^2/2)) with E_e = 6.0 GeV. U21: E1 = 8.36 keV at K = 1.38, so 70 keV is about the 7th harmonic at K of about 1.1 (computed). Only odd harmonics on axis. The 0.136% electron energy spread broadens high harmonics strongly (Tanaka-Kitamura factor at n x N x sigma_E). Planned SCU vs pre-upgrade SCU1: 530x brilliance (r5, r12, r35).

interactiveIdeas.title: Why the hutch looks like a step pyramid
interactiveIdeas.concept: Cutaway of 20-ID-E. Light up the 1 A, 40 keV Debye cone from the sample and watch it fill the tall, wide back half and hit the D4 wall. A slider changes the energy or d-spacing and the cone shrinks or grows.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: Building shapes follow physics: the back half is 10.8 m wide and 6.9 m tall so an 18 deg cone fits.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: 2-theta = 2 asin(lambda/2d) is 17.8 deg for d = 1 A at 40 keV. Radius = L tan(2-theta) is about 5.3 m at L of about 16.4 m. Beam height 1.4 m, so only the upper half-cone reaches the wall (r28, r29).

interactiveIdeas.title: Ride along with a radioactive sample
interactiveIdeas.concept: Step-by-step journey: reactor component, then shipping cask, AML glove box, encapsulation, transfer cart to 20-ID-E, HEDM scan and return. Dose-rate counters update along the way.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: How a long beamline and a dedicated lab make it safe to study irradiated materials with X-rays.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Limit 100 mrem/h beta/gamma at 30 cm. At least one containment layer. Containment walls must be X-ray transparent at 60-100 keV; the 1/e length is about mm in steel and Zr. Higher-dose samples go preferentially to 20-ID, outside the main hall (r18).

funFacts: At about 20 m long, 20-ID-E is 'the largest enclosure we've built at the APS' (r21).
HEXM's main hutch stands in its own building, the Long Beamline Building. Its groundbreaking on July 22, 2020 was described as 'the only externally visible part of the APS Upgrade' (r22).
The X-rays travel about 180 m (590 ft) to the sample, roughly 2.3 times the 'more typical 80 meters', and arrive about 0.6 microseconds after leaving the electron beam (r20; travel time computed).
Building HEXM meant removing offices in lab-office Building 436 and adding a new corridor of 14 offices along the beam pipe (r23).
The long beamlines cut the walkway around the APS ring at sectors 19-20. Stairs and an elevator now carry people over the beam pipes, ending the tradition of a full lap on foot or tricycle (r15).
The back half of 20-ID-E is 10.8 m wide and 6.9 m tall so that X-rays scattered at 18 degrees can still land on a detector 16 m away (r28).
Energy Secretary Chris Wright placed HEXM's inaugural sample, a piece of a jet-engine turbine blade, in July 2025 (r14).
The high-throughput HEDM instrument in 20-ID-D was built by four universities with NSF funding: 'many places with wading pools... this instrument... will be an Olympic swimming pool' (r24, r25).

Before HEXM, sector 20 hosted X-ray spectroscopy for more than 25 years (about 600 papers). That program moved to 25-ID in 2022, and the sector's history goes back to the Pacific Northwest Consortium CAT formed in 1990 (r26, r27).
HEXM's hutch sits on a 12-inch concrete slab; its long-beamline neighbor ISN needed 39 inches for vibration control (r23).
Next door is a lab built to handle radioactive samples; its first users studied stainless-steel parts retired from a nuclear reactor after decades of service (r19).
Before the upgrade, only about 1 in 100,000 photons at HEDM energies was spatially coherent, which made high-energy coherent imaging impractical (r7).
'HEXM will be the only beamline worldwide to offer dark-field X-ray microscopy at high energies' (Ashley Bucsek, University of Michigan, r20).
The design calls for a laser tracker (Leica Absolute Tracker class) to watch where the 100 kg detectors are inside the hutch (r28).

openQuestions: Exact first-light date not published. Monthly charts show stage 2 (installation complete) in Dec 2024 and Jan 2025, stage 3 (ops commissioning) on 10 Mar 2025 and stage 5 by July 2025 (r13, r14). The July 2025 AML report says shielding verification happened 'in 2025' (r18). First light is therefore bracketed between late Jan and Jul 2025, most likely by Mar 2025.

Status conflict: the 5 Oct 2026 chart shows stage 6 (general users) and the Proposal Types page lists 20-ID-D,E for GU proposals, but the Beamline Directory still says 'Commissioning' (likely stale) (r13, r16, r9).

Source: interim permanent-magnet U21 + U21/U25 revolver as of 22 Sep 2026 (r12). The SCU baseline changed from about 3.5-3.8 m total (FDR 4-4, Kmax 1.63) to 2 x 1.9 m in one cryostat (FDR Ch3, Strategic Plan). Installation is planned for 2026-2027 after core-reliability problems (r1, r3, r17). The Beamline Directory specs (1e14 ph/s at 70 keV) assume the SCU and have not been measured with the interim source.
Front-end window material: 0.5 mm Be (FDR 4-4.3 and the Table 4.27 note) vs 'Diamond Window' (FDR Table 4.28). As-built not confirmed.

Which refractive optics (L1-L7) are installed as of 2026 is unclear. The FDR lists most lens sets as 'Not in Project Scope' (R&D). The AML report (Jul 2025) confirms 'refractive-based focusing optics' in 20-ID-A without details (r18). Shastri & Antipov (JSR 2026) describe diamond lenses for collimation into a high-resolution monochromator, focusing for coherent diffraction 'on a long beamline' and a convex beam-expander test at 40-70 keV (abstract via Europe PMC). The full text is Cloudflare-blocked, so lens positions, focal lengths and which beamline was used are unverified (r39).

As-built detector suite: the Directory lists a Varex 4343 and a SpectrumLogic 3131HS (station not specified). The D3 specification used a Pilatus3 X CdTe 6M as reference, KA Imaging claims BrillianSe a-Se detectors, and D4 (ESD-011) details are unpublished. 'SpectrumLogic 3131HS' specs could not be verified.
BCDI and DFXM operational status for users is unknown: the AML report lists BCDI as available at 20-ID-E, but no published HEXM BCDI/DFXM result was found (r18).
The 2017 PDR XMAT in situ ion-irradiation source ('20-30 m of space' next to the C/E station) is not mentioned in later documents; presumably not built.

Enclosure extents for 20-ID-A, -B, -C and -D were scaled from the 2019 FDR layout figure (about +/-0.5 m) and may differ from as-built. 20-ID-E dimensions come from the 2021 ESD and match the 64'-11" x 35'-5" in FDR Fig. 4.1.
Sample position: 180.7 m (FDR Table 4.28) vs about 180.9 m implied by ESD-010 (3.5 m from the upstream wall at about 177.4 m).
Upper energy limit: 120 keV (FDR, Directory) vs 140 keV (D3 ESD photon-delivery statement).
Station naming changed: the PDR (2017) used A/B/C; the FDR and as-built use 20-ID-A, -D and -E. Legacy 20-ID-B/C remain in the hall but are unused (r11).
The beamline used for the first AML user experiment (Feb 2026 DOE article) was not stated: 1-ID or 20-ID (r19).
FDR Table 4.29 labels all beam sizes as um, but the 'unfocused' rows (2.5 x 2.2 at E; 1 x 0.9 at D) must be mm (confirmed by the Beamline Directory).
